Threat: Forge an identity through weak token or session verification
Prerequisite: Know the published demo configuration or send an unsigned API token
Fix: Reject unsigned tokens; use a tested verifier; use independent random signing keys; expire sessions

Threat: Change the login SQL through user input
Fix: Use a parameterized login query; verify a password hash; use a restricted DB role

Threat: Read or change grades outside the user's scope
Prerequisite: Have a student or teacher identity
Fix: Check note ownership and teacher class ownership on API reads; writes; pages; exports

Threat: Read private comments from a copied database
Prerequisite: Obtain database files or a backup copy
Fix: Encrypt comments with AES-GCM; keep the key separate; control backup retention
Status: Plaintext schema confirmed; theft not simulated

Threat: Execute shell commands through Admin Ping
Prerequisite: Have an admin session or compromise it
Fix: Remove shell execution; pass a fixed argument list; validate the host; reduce OS privileges

Threat: Run active content through a stored comment
Prerequisite: Write a comment that a victim later reads
Fix: Keep HTML autoescape enabled; use an allowlist sanitizer only when rich text is required

Threat: Submit a state change from another website
Prerequisite: The victim has a live teacher or admin browser session
Fix: Validate CSRF tokens on every state-changing request; set appropriate cookie attributes
Status: No CSRF check in route; browser attack not run

Threat: Deny or alter a sensitive action record
Prerequisite: Have access to weak logs or act through an identity that cannot be trusted
Fix: Record actor; action; target; result; before/after values; protect audit storage
Status: Audit gaps confirmed; log alteration not run

Threat: Recover passwords or credentials from stored material
Prerequisite: Read the course image, its bundled backup, or a copied user table
Fix: Hash user passwords; remove bundled credential backups; restrict file and secret access
Status: Storage design confirmed; no credential attack run

Threat: Read credentials or session data on an HTTP path
Prerequisite: Control a network path between a browser and the published HTTP port
Fix: Use authenticated HTTPS for network use; protect session cookies
Status: HTTP on all host interfaces in Compose; interception not run

Threat: Read database traffic without DB TLS
Prerequisite: Control a transport path to the DB
Fix: Use verified DB TLS where the network is not trusted; restrict DB connectivity
Status: Configuration confirmed; packet capture not run

Threat: Exhaust the app or DB with repeated expensive requests
Prerequisite: Access a permitted request path or the published DB port
Fix: Set rate and request limits; use pagination; bound DB work; add timeouts

Threat: Expose implementation details through errors or debug mode
Prerequisite: Trigger an error on a reachable course route
Fix: Disable the debugger; return generic errors; keep detailed diagnostics in protected logs
Status: Source confirms debug and detailed errors; debugger not tested

Threat: Use the application DB login with excessive DB authority
Prerequisite: Execute attacker-controlled SQL through the application, for example R02
Fix: Use a non-superuser app role with only the required table and sequence grants
Status: Role flags confirmed; privileged operation not run

Threat: Log in to PostgreSQL directly through the published port
Prerequisite: Reach TCP 5432 on the host; the password is in the public Compose file
Fix: Remove the published DB port; keep the DB on an internal network; keep the DB password outside the repository; use a non-superuser app role
Status: Configuration confirmed; remote DB login not attempted

Threat: Take control of the Docker host through the mounted Docker socket or project tree
Prerequisite: Run a command in the web container, for example through R05
Fix: Remove the Docker socket and project-tree mounts; run the web container as a non-root user; drop Linux capabilities
Status: Configuration confirmed; host access not attempted

Threat: Use Admin Ping to probe internal hosts or send traffic to other networks
Prerequisite: Have an admin session or compromise it
Fix: Allow only approved Ping targets; block internal and link-local ranges; rate-limit Ping requests

Threat: Return false Ping results through spoofed DNS or ICMP replies
Prerequisite: Control DNS resolution or the network path to the target
Fix: Treat Ping output only as a hint; prefer IP targets or verified DNS; confirm service health with an authenticated check
